newsitem.title: UK: Hamleys says sales begin 97 in line with 96.
newsitem.headline: Hamleys says sales begin 97 in line with 96.

text.p: British toy group Hamleys Plc said on Tuesday like-for-like sales began the year in line with last year, but it remains confident of continued improvement in its businesses in 1997.

"We remain confident that 1997 will continue the improvement in both the Hamleys' and House of Toys' businesses, although like-for-like sales have started the year in line with last year's," chairman Howard Dyer said in a statement accompanying the annual results.
He said the level of tourism this summer and its impact on the Regent Street store in London was hard to predict owing to the continued strength of sterling.
The profitability of the Hamleys' chain of shops increased by 11 percent on the year.

Earlier this month Hamleys announced that it was opening 23 units of its House of Toys' operation at Debenhams centres on a year round basis, with a further 28 units operating during the Christmas period. Debenhams is owned by Burton Group.
"The expansion into Debenhams should enhance profitability in 1997 and make a more significant contribution the following year once we have established the business," said Dyer.

The group is withdrawing the House of Toys' operation from House of Frazer stores. Sales from operations within House of Frazer were lower last year as it traded from fewer outlets. But this shortfall was "partially compensated" by new units within John Menzies in Edinburgh and Arnotts in Dublin.
Dyer said the group's own-brand development would continue, "allowing the business to expand overseas with further franchise operations and joint venture initiatives at airports".
Earlier, Hamleys reported an eight percent jump in pre-tax profits to 6.88 million stg from 6.38 million the year before and a rise in the total dividend to nine pence per share from 8.1 pence.
